text:
maria: heads up — saw a ~30% p99 latency spike for runtime-prod around 12:10 UTC, throughput dropped ~15%. Not obvious in the per-route dashboard, digging in now.
kevin: ack, which hosts/instance groups?
maria: concentrated on gpu-pool-3, node set: gpu-3a. Logs show a flurry of KV cache evictions + kernel selection warnings.
perf-bot: alert - runtime.kernel_fallback_rate high on cluster gpu-pool-3 (0.027) at 12:09:47 UTC :rotating_light:
autoscaler-bot: evicted instance i-0a1b2c3d from gpu-pool-3 due to host memory pressure
sam: can you paste the kernel warning lines?
maria: sure, snippet below:
```
2026-03-18T12:09:46Z WARN runtime.kernel_selector: selected fallback kernel for model=redwood-7b q8_0 due to heuristics mismatch (expected seq=64 saw 256)
2026-03-18T12:09:46Z INFO kvcache: eviction count=482 host=gpu-3a-7
2026-03-18T12:09:47Z DEBUG batching: flush due to burst, batch_size=1
```
kevin: that expected-vs-observed seq mismatch looks like an input distribution change — maybe client started sending long-context requests. Any recent rollout?
ryan: there was a small heuristic tweak to batching logic in yesterday's canary, it relied more on predicted seq len for kernel selection.
maria: can confirm canary % is low but some traffic routed to it for gpu-pool-3. However the bigger problem is observability — traces are sparse. Only ~40% of requests have runtime spans at spike time. Logs have x-trace ids but they don't surface in tracing UI.
sam: hmm, we recently reduced trace sampling on high-throughput hosts to 0.05 to save costs. Might have been applied too aggressively to gpu pool.
kevin: prom queries I ran: `sum(rate(runtime_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le)` shows p99 bump but `sum(runtime_kernel_fallback_total)` is too coarse — missing kernel labels in the metric for some hosts (label `kernel_name` gone). Dashboard mismatch.
ryan: that explains dashboard mismatch — fallback metric ingestion change in the exporter removed `kernel_name` when fallback path used a legacy code path. Oops.
perf-bot: note created - perf/1782103456: investigate kernel-selection fallback + trace sampling + kv evict correlation
maria: quick mitigation ideas: 1) roll back batching heuristic canary to prior version for gpu-pool-3 2) increase trace sampling on affected hosts from 5% -> 20% for next 30m 3) bump log sampling for runtime to capture full traces (temporarily) 4) add kernel_fallback_rate alert with per-host label.
sam: I'm on (2) and (3) now. Pushing tracing config to gpu-3a hosts.
kevin: I'll prepare rollback PR for batching canary, mark for hotfix.
ryan: I'll fix exporter to restore `kernel_name` label when fallback path triggers, and reopen metric backlog for the missing time range.
maria: also want a short profiler run on a repro host to confirm slow kernel path — `python -m cProfile` produced a hot path in `attention_kernel_slow` during initial test. Sam can you run `perf record` on gpu-3a-7?
sam: yep running perf + nvprof now, will upload flamegraph link here.
kevin: action owners: kevin (rollback), sam (sampling/logs + profile), ryan (metrics exporter fix), maria (incident coord + RCA doc).
ryan: follow-up items: add a dashboard panel that compares `kernel_fallback_rate` with `kv_evictions` and `trace_ingestion_rate` so we can spot this combo quickly.
maria: thanks. ETA on rollback PR?
kevin: 20m. rolling back canary in staging now, will promote hotfix after smoke.
maria: noted. after rollback and increased sampling let's re-evaluate p99 in 15m and then draft a short postmortem for observability gaps.
perf-bot: update - hotfix promoted to gpu-pool-3 staging at 12:27 UTC, smoke passed.
maria: great — leaving this thread open until we confirm stabilization and have the RCA doc.
kevin: stabilization looks good so far, p99 trending down.
sam: uploaded flamegraph: https://internal-s3.company/flamegraphs/1782103456/gpu-3a-7.svg (shows heavy time in attention_kernel_slow with extra memcpy)
ryan: exporter PR opened: restore kernel_name label and backfill metrics. PR: https://git.company/repo/pull/4321
maria: will start RCA doc in docs/incident-reports and link here when ready. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
